chosen.premise: Tangela can lose its vines painlessly, then regrow the missing vines by the very next day.
chosen.hook: Grab Tangela’s vines, and they grow back tomorrow.
chosen.visualIdea: Show vines snapping away without pain, followed by a day-night time-lapse of fresh vines returning.
chosen.note: A precise, unusual biological rule with a strong contradiction: the vines can be removed painlessly and return by the next day. The time-lapse is immediately visual.

candidates.premise: Tangela’s blue vines keep growing for its entire life, even after torn vines are removed.
candidates.hook: Tangela’s vines never stop growing—even when torn off.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate vines continuously lengthening, then regrowing over the spots where they were torn away.
candidates.note: Excellent Tangela-only premise and highly visual, though “never stop” and “regrow after removal” overlap somewhat with the stronger next-day-regrowth angle and lack its exact time marker.

candidates.premise: Tangela’s vines completely hide its identity, and no one has ever seen the face beneath them.
candidates.hook: Tangela’s face has never been seen.
candidates.visualIdea: Zoom through layers of blue vines toward a silhouette, then stop before revealing what is underneath.
candidates.note: Very Tangela-specific and visually strong, but “no one has ever seen the face” is a familiar mystery premise and offers less concrete payoff.

candidates.premise: Tangela’s vines are useful beyond battle: they are used as herbs in Galar and as a refreshing spice in Hisui.
candidates.hook: Tangela’s vines can end up in food.
candidates.visualIdea: Split the screen between Galar herbs and Hisui seasoning, both sourced from Tangela’s blue vines.
candidates.note: Unexpected and well supported, with a useful regional comparison. The food-use visual is clear, though the premise is less instantly dramatic than regrowth.

candidates.premise: Tangela’s fine-haired vines make anything caught in them feel ticklish while the vines keep moving.
candidates.hook: Tangela’s trap is a tickle attack.
candidates.visualIdea: A moving vine snare catches an approaching object, with playful vibration lines showing the ticklish effect.
candidates.note: The ticklish trap is memorable and visual, but the evidence describes being ticklish when ensnared rather than clearly establishing it as a deliberate defensive attack.

candidates.premise: Tangela evolves into Tangrowth only when it levels up while knowing Ancient Power.
candidates.hook: Tangela needs one specific move to evolve.
candidates.visualIdea: Display Tangela, the Ancient Power move requirement, and a level-up transition into Tangrowth.
candidates.note: Concrete and useful for players, but evolution-by-move is not unique to Tangela and the cited method comes from secondary data rather than the Pokédex entries.

rounds.request: A stronger angle would need an equally Tangela-specific rule with a sharper contradiction, an exact measurable detail, and a visual transformation that is better supported by the research.
